angle: engineering: audit the cycle-1 recommendation before trusting it
summary: Investigating cycle 1's own recommendation ('the idealized-fractional numbers already equal the $20-notional-cap numbers') found it was WRONG: bus/fleet/lev-backtest-engine.js simulate()'s fractional branch never referenced the `cap` option at all -- it sized every entry off compounding equityAtOpen, unbounded. Verified empirically (a $1000 account with cap=20 bought the full $1000). Fixed: fractional entries now capped at min(cap,w*equityAtOpen), continuous; a second, related bug found while fixing the first -- the same cap was being applied to the buy-and-hold BENCHMARK too, degenerating it into a single capped entry + idle cash instead of a true fully-invested reference; fixed by giving benchmarks cap:Infinity. Added 2 regression tests (34->35, both fail against the pre-fix code, confirmed by reconstructing it in a scratch copy). Reran --descriptive with the fix: verdict flips from INCONCLUSIVE to FAIL -- S1 and S2 on QQQ->TQQQ no longer beat plain buy-and-hold QQQ CAGR after costs (13.9%/15.2% vs 15.5%) once sizing correctly reflects C1's real $20 cap and the benchmark is correctly uncapped. This corrects an earlier wrong claim made to the owner (that the strategy was 'achievable and promising' for C1).

angle: cap sensitivity: is the $20 per-entry cap (not the trend rules) what makes S1/S2 lose to buy-and-hold QQQ?
summary: Added --cap <dollars> to backtest-lev-trend.js --descriptive (sensitivity only; refuses with --tune/--test; writes <report>.capN.md with a SENSITIVITY banner; default run unchanged). Regression test written first and shown to fail before the feature, and to fail again with the cap parsed but not wired to the simulator (696.4 vs 696.4). 36/36 selftest, 161/161 suite. Real sweep, QQQ->TQQQ full span 2021-08..2026-09 (5 bps / 15 bps): cap $20 S1 13.9% S2 15.2% CAGR (FAIL vs QQQ 15.5%); cap $30 S1 17.8%/17.8% maxDD 34.8%, S2 19.6%/18.1% maxDD 29.9-31.0% -- S1's drawdown matches QQQ's 35.0% so this is a risk-matched win, not just more leverage; cap $40 S1 21.3% S2 23.1% (maxDD 44.7%/38.1%, above QQQ); cap $50 S1 22.2% S2 25.0% (maxDD 50.6%/42.7%). Conclusion: the cap, not the rules, caused the FAIL. Caveats: one ~5-year sample whose edge comes mostly from sidestepping 2022, S1 has 3 trades, S2 113 (cost-sensitive), 3 caps tried (mild snooping), earlier deflated Sharpe ~0.2-0.3 (not significant), no 2008-style stress. Raising C1's cap is a protected budget-envelope policy change: owner's call, not recommended on this evidence alone; longer data first.

angle: longer free data: FMP connector, then Alpaca SIP feed
summary: FMP (owner's connected MCP): REJECTED -- free plan denies ETF symbols (QQQ/TQQQ) and any date filter; stocks only ~5y (AAPL 1254 rows from 2021-09-30), shorter than what we already have. Alpaca SIP feed on the existing free paper keys: WORKS, QQQ history from 2016-01-04 (IEX only from 2020-07-27). Built test-first: lev-bars-cache.js --feed iex|sip (default iex unchanged; sip sends a past end date; own cache dir bus/fleet/data/lev-bars-sip/, source alpaca-sip; unknown feed refused before any fetch); 2 new checks failed before, 13/13 after. Real fetch: 8 symbols x 2699 bars 2016-01-04..2026-09-28, 0 missing trading days, no sanity flags. SIP vs IEX on the 2020-07-27..2026-09-25 overlap (close-to-close): QQQ/SPY/BIL/SHY mean abs daily diff 0.007-0.03%; leveraged ETFs 0.13-0.19% with 2-4 days >2% (IEX thin prints, worst 2024-12-24 half day); end-of-overlap price ratio ~1.000 (no adjustment drift). SIP is the better source. Unlocks a genuinely unseen window (2017-2021-08, incl. 2018 Q4 and the 2020 crash) for the canonical rules.
